assets.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE original transparent fantasy strategy overworld town sprite. The supplied OLD FACTION ART is an identity reference. Rebuild it creatively into a distinct faction settlement with the construction system specified below.
SHARED MAP CONSTRAINTS ONLY: elevated orthographic camera looking down about 45 degrees, looking toward the town from the south with entrance facing viewer. Broad 5-column by 3-ground-row footprint. Overall painted width about 1.25-1.4 times total painted height. One obvious, human-scale main entrance EXACTLY at the front/bottom horizontal center, its dry threshold at the lowest central ground contact. Short flush threshold, no projecting road or long approach bridge. Asymmetric interior layout and distinctive silhouette. Scale is a substantial dense settlement, not a small isolated building; small doors/windows communicate scale.
ART: finely detailed, weathered hand-painted/pre-rendered late-1990s adventure-map raster art, realistic small materials, upper-left soft daylight, restrained speculars. Readable at 240px displayed width. Fine granular detail, natural shadows, no smooth glossy/mobile-game icon rendering.
TERRAIN NEUTRAL: structural footings only, cutout edges, no background or surrounding ground patch, no water/sea/swamp/mud/sand/grass island/snow/lava, no external cast shadow. Vegetation may be part of Thornwake buildings, never a landscape base. Actual RGBA alpha transparency. Square output; leave 7% transparent margin. NO painted flags, pennants, banners, heraldry, sails with insignia, text, characters, UI or grid. Runtime ownership flags are added later.
CRITICAL DESIGN INDEPENDENCE: do NOT use a generic European castle, repeating curtain wall, battlements, symmetrical gatehouse towers, cathedral-and-houses arrangement or terraced stone courtyard castle template. These are original factions with different engineering. Camera and entrance placement do not mean shared buildings. The town MUST follow its specific construction and silhouette:
MIRECLAW COVENANT — predatory ferry clans, drum law and bogplate handlers. A low sprawling raider settlement built from bundles of dark timber pilings, lashed reed-and-hide dens, rusty ferry chains, woven shell-shaped roofs, bone tokens and irregular plank decks. The largest building is a long low arched reed den toward the LEFT REAR, with an exposed large ritual drum frame nearby. Rounded and crouched building forms. At right, rough timber ferry-chain winches and a squat mudglass shrine give a completely different silhouette; short antler/harpoon lookout frames rather than tall roofed towers. Several interlinked den compounds, rope walkways and equipment sheds, small muted green peatwax lanterns. Front-center entrance is a low open break in the rough palisade between two chain-winches and bone posts, a flat dry plank sill. No masonry ramparts, paved medieval terraces, stone towers or pointed European roof houses. Rust, green-black wood, yellow reed and dull bone. Platforms rest on visible short solid pilings and dry stone shoes without any water, weeds or mud below. Dense asymmetrical low town with open working decks; architecture communicates ferry logistics and oral clan rites.
assets.accessible_description: Low reed-and-hide den compounds, bone tokens, ferry-chain winches and an exposed ritual drum on dry timber pilings; front entrance between chain posts.
assets.entrance_registration: Visually selected front-center doorway threshold, verified against the source alpha; lower supporting roots, posts and wheels are excluded from the entrance anchor.
